notes:
Dark Knight AF2. The one thing worth getting right here is the key item's NAME: res/key_items.lua 235 is literally '"Darksteel Formula"' WITH the double quotes as part of the string, and the wiki writes it the same way in both the Item Reqs line and bullet 6. The unquoted form does not resolve, so the quotes are kept -- dropping them would cost step 7 its evidence.

Bullet 4 ('obtain a Yagudo Cherry from a vendor or the AH') is deliberately NOT its own step. A Yagudo Cherry is a cheap, common vendor item; making holding one the evidence for a rung would jump the mark to the Giddeus trade for anybody who happens to have one in the satchel. It is merged into the trade step as its requirement instead, with the sourcing in the note. The Letter and the Formula are the two honest anchors, and they bracket the whole middle of the quest.

Bullet 6 is a fight and then a second click on the same ???, so it splits into two steps that both carry bullet 6. Bullet 7 is the page's own '(Optional)' -- extra dialogue only. The unnumbered line after bullet 1 ('the rest can be done on any job') is a note on the job gate, not a step.

notes:
Five bullets, five steps, and every one of them is a real action -- unusually clean. The three Peculiar Rootprints are explicitly ORDERED ('Then...', 'Afterwards, touch the third and final...'), so they are three ordered rungs and NOT a group; grouping them would draw all three at once and tell the player something the page contradicts. They share a target name and are separated only by zone, which is exactly what the per-step zone field is for -- and 'Peculiar Rootprints' resolves as a real markable entity, so all three carry markers.

All three zones are Wings of the Goddess past versions, and the (S) suffix resolves correctly (91, 88, 97), so it is kept as the wiki writes it. Every sub-bullet is travel advice -- Survival Guides, Campaign Arbiter warps, Recall-Meriph -- and none is a step. Windurst Waters (North) is one half of zone 238, so the start zone is plain Windurst Waters. Nothing in this quest is observable: no key item, no item, no count, so every evidence field is null.

notes:
The page contradicts itself about where the reward comes from. Bullet 6 says returning to Kohlo-Lakolo sends you to the House of the Hero in Windurst Walls (G-3) 'for your reward'; bullet 7 says zone and return to Kohlo-Lakolo 'to receive your reward'. Both are kept, in that order, on the reading that the House of the Hero is a cutscene stop and Kohlo-Lakolo actually hands over the Bouncer Club -- but the quest is demoted to medium for it rather than picking one and hiding the other.

Bullets 3 and 4 are the trap-door sequence in Castle Oztroja, and the page names NOTHING you can target: 'the door at (I-8)' and 'the handles in front of the door' are descriptions, not entity names, so the target is none and the grid carries the information instead. Bullet 5's Blank Target IS named, and is recorded even though it is the same OBJECT_DENY entity that costs Divine Might its markers -- it keeps the rung and the Old ring evidence, which is the one real anchor in the quest. Old ring resolves as a KEY ITEM (130), not an item; the item table has no such entry, so getting the kind wrong here would silently cost the anchor.

Bullet 1 ('zone after the previous quest') is a precondition folded into step 1's note, and the sub-bullet about already holding the ring is a shortcut, not a step. The sub-bullet under 6 -- that taking too long ends the quest at Kohlo-Lakolo with no House of the Hero trip at all -- is a genuine alternate branch that the ladder cannot express, hence or_branch_unmodelled.

notes:
The Ebisu rod quest, and the interesting problem here is that the quest does not exist in your log until you have BOUGHT the Serpent Rumors key item from Fennella in Port Windurst (C-8) -- 95,000 Guild Points at Fishing rank Adept or higher. That is bullet 1, it is a real interaction with a real markable NPC, and it is step 1 even though the header's giver is Irmilant in Rabao. Irmilant is kept as start.raw and start.npc because he is the header's giver and steps 4 to 6 are all his; Fennella is flagged rather than promoted.

THE FISHING RANK IS NOW A GATE. gates.craft records `Fishing rank Adept`, which resolves to res/skills.lua 48 and res/synth_ranks.lua 8. The page is quoted verbatim -- "To begin this quest in your log, you need the Serpent Rumors key item. It can be purchased from Fennella in Port Windurst (C-8) for 95,000 Guild Points with Fishing rank Adept or higher." -- and "to begin this quest in your log" is what makes it an ENTRY condition rather than a mid-quest cost: the rank gates the purchase, the purchase gates the quest existing at all. Before this the entry evaluated to `ready` with zero reasons, so every character below Adept saw a yellow "!" on Fennella inviting a trip to Port Windurst for something they cannot buy.

THE 95,000 GUILD POINTS ARE OBSERVABLE TOO, and the first attempt at this record said they were not. That claim came from a grep for "guild" that found only shop traffic -- 0x083/0x085 inventory and sale lists and a 'Craft Rank' field at 0x03C:0C saying which rank may buy a product -- and stopped there. Packet 0x113 'Currency Info' (fields.lua:3855) carries nine signed ints starting at offset 0x20, one per guild, in res/skills.lua id order for ids 48 to 56; Fishing is the first. It is recorded here as a mistake rather than quietly corrected, because it is exactly the inherited-claim failure this pass exists to fix, committed while fixing one. Both halves of the price are now gates: skill 48 rank 8, and 95,000 points in guild 48. Synergy (57) has no guild-point counter at all -- 0x44 is Cinders -- so a points gate on it is refused by validate.py rather than read off the end of the block.

Bullet 2 is TWO independent appraisal loops at the same NPC -- Liks give Opal Silk, Gugrusaurus gives Saber Shoot, at roughly half a percent each -- so it is two steps sharing a group rather than one step with a misleading AND-list of both fish. The page never says where Zaldon is, and hard rule 1 forbids supplying it, so both steps have a null zone; Zaldon resolves unambiguously so the marker survives anyway.

Bullet 1's sub-bullet says the other items can be farmed before the quest is initiated, so steps 1 to 3 are only loosely ordered; they are left in page order because the Serpent Rumors purchase is what makes the quest real. Bullet 5's conquest tally wait is unobservable. The 'After the walkthrough: Notes' section is NOT steps -- it is how to replace an Ebisu Fishing Rod you dropped by mistake, after the quest is already over, and the Takitaro in it is deliberately absent from the ladder.

notes:
Four rungs, no key items, no items, nothing observable anywhere in the quest -- every evidence field is null and that is the honest answer, not a gap. The reward is experience and Bayld, which is not evidence of anything.

The object in bullet 4 is the problem. The page writes it as 'the Ergon Locus ???' and then warns in the same breath that it 'should not be confused with the regular Ergon Locus'. 'Ergon Locus' does resolve as a real entity, so it is used rather than recording a bare ??? that could never carry a marker -- but that means the marker may equally find the ordinary Ergon Locus in the same zone, which is why that step is medium and the whole quest is medium. The grid (I-8) and the approach note are what actually separate them for the player: you must come from (H-8) and specifically NOT from (I-7).

Bullet 3 is merged into bullet 4's step: it names no target of its own, only two Bivouac routes into Yorcia Weald, so a separate travel rung would be a position the player cannot be tracked through for no gain. The header gives Rigobertine no grid; (J-8) is taken from bullet 1 and the header string is preserved verbatim in start.raw. The page carries the wiki's own [unverified] tag on the claim that the blocking bush was removed in the August 2025 update; that is a note about the approach, not a step, and not a time gate any more.

notes:
A short repeatable cruor quest, and the one place in this batch where items_alt earns its keep: bullet 3's Apple Pie and its sub-bullet's Apple Pie +1 are two genuinely independent ways to satisfy the same optional step -- the +1 only changes the flavour text -- so the pie is items and the +1 is items_alt, not an AND-list of both. The step is the page's own 'Optional:' and is marked so; it exists purely to make Yurim remember what she wanted, and the quest can be finished without it.

Bullet 2 is not a step -- it is her forgetting, which is the reason the pie exists. Bullet 4 is a step even though it is written as a bare fact about where the mobs are: killing Escarp Murex at (J-7) is how you get the Murex Spicule, which is the quest's only anchor and a drop nobody carries by accident. The 25-completions fame note and the closing 'zoning is required to repeat' line are cooldown and repeat mechanics, not steps.

Fame 'amis' is an Abyssea zone code, not one of the nine regions, so it gates nothing. The header's Empyrean +1 leg seals are a reward table and are absent from the ladder.
